hints.title: Pairwise Comparison Obstacle
hints.text: Comparing each string against all others requires quadratic comparisons. What canonical representation or signature can you compute for any string so that all its anagrams share that exact representation?

hints.title: Unique Key Representation
hints.text: Anagrams have identical character frequencies. Sorting the characters of a word or encoding its 26-element character count creates a unique key that groups matching words together.

hints.title: Map by Signature Key
hints.text: Iterate through each word in the list. Compute its canonical key by sorting its characters or encoding character counts. Map each unique key to a list of original words. Finally, collect and return all the lists of grouped words.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: K: maximum length of a string in strs (0 <= K <= 100)
complexity.notes: Counting 26 characters for each string takes O(K) time per word, totaling O(N * K) time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Pairwise anagram checking takes O(N^2 * K) time. For N = 10^4, N^2 = 10^8 comparisons, causing time limit exceeded.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing string groups in memory requires O(N * K) space to store all words in buckets, but reduces time from O(N^2 * K) to linear O(N * K).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clear choice of canonical key (count tuple of size 26 or sorted string), handling empty strings and single characters, returning values in any order.
